corrections.issue: Speaker and meaning are muddled: the quote is the host reading out Bessent's earlier remark (Capital Allocators, Nov 2024) and the 'now judges what delivers rather than what is priced' half is the host's premise, which Bessent rejected in his reply ('there is information value in the market').
corrections.fix: Host quotes Bessent's own Abenomics line, 'I have no idea [whether it will work], but it will be the market ride of a lifetime': a large policy shift can drive large price moves whether or not the policy works; as policymaker Bessent says he still finds information value in market prices.

corrections.issue: Overstates the catalyst: Bessent says the current account turned to deficit after the reactors were switched off 'but nothing really happened' and the yen stayed in a 78-83 range; the shutdown was a candidate catalyst that did not move the price, and he put the trade back on the shelf until Abe and the BoJ board seats appeared.
corrections.fix: After Fukushima the nuclear shutdown forced fuel imports and pushed Japan's ~3% of GDP current account surplus into deficit, which looked like a possible yen-short catalyst, but the yen did not move (78-83) until the Abe/BoJ catalyst.

corrections.issue: Lumps gold revaluation with balance-sheet shrinkage: asked whether revaluing gold and sterilising could let the Fed shed assets, Bessent answered that the two are 'very very independent'; the advance-signalling and reserve-regime points apply to the Fed's balance sheet only.
corrections.fix: Bessent separates gold revaluation from balance-sheet reduction (independent); shrinking the Fed balance sheet or moving between reserve regimes would need signalling well in advance and a review of how post-GFC regulation raised reserve demand versus a skinnier-reserve, interbank model.

completeness_estimate: 0.80 - first reader caught the investing principles, the yen/Abenomics trade and most policy statements (about 45 of roughly 57 ideas); missed the Fed/BoE and debt-management exchange, tariff communication, and coalition/path-dependence geopolitics; also overstated the Fukushima current-account catalyst (corrected)
